survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a country note summarising indicators from OECD’s Education at a Glance 2025 rather than analysing student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS). As such, it does not specify a student-level sampling frame, replicate design, or any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) for an analytic model. The figures and tables referenced (e.g., unemployment rates, wage gaps, enrolment, expenditure, teacher indicators) are compiled from OECD indicator production processes and administrative/statistical sources, with indicator-specific methodologies described in the companion “Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes” publication. For any re-use at the microdata level, analysts would need to consult the underlying indicator methodology for each measure; this note itself does not provide weighting or PV/scaling instructions for model-based inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this country note does not report student-level cognitive achievement scores from an ILSA with PV-based scaling; it reports descriptive education-system indicators (e.g., educational attainment, unemployment by attainment, enrolment rates, expenditure per student, teacher vacancy/turnover). Missing-data handling is not reported here because the note does not present an estimation model with an explicit missing-data procedure; instead, it summarises already-produced OECD indicators. The detailed indicator-specific data collection and processing rules are provided in the companion OECD technical documentation referenced in the text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is not an ILSA microdata analysis; it is a descriptive country note using the latest available OECD Education at a Glance 2025 indicators for Argentina. The note does not define an analytic subsample of students (e.g., grade band, assessment module, or case exclusions). Therefore, the analytic sample is not specified at the student level in this document; users should refer to the Education at a Glance 2025 indicator tables and the “Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes” for measure-specific inclusion criteria.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Argentina summarises system-level education indicators rather than estimating student-level relationships using ML. It highlights tertiary attainment (19% among 25–34 year-olds in 2024), unemployment patterns by educational attainment (e.g., 4.1% unemployment for tertiary-educated young adults in Argentina in 2023), and wage gaps by attainment (e.g., 13% gap for upper secondary vs below upper secondary; 63% gap for tertiary vs upper secondary in 2023). It also reports participation in early childhood education (ISCED 0 rising from 73% to 77% between 2013 and 2023), repetition rates in lower secondary (down to 5.5% in 2023), and tertiary field-of-study shares (e.g., 16% STEM among bachelor’s graduates). The note further covers education financing (expenditure per student and tertiary vs non-tertiary differences), teacher workforce indicators (vacancies and turnover), and school calendar structure. Because it is descriptive and indicator-based, it does not provide PV handling, missing-data procedures, or model performance metrics for predictive inference.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to ILSA/ML methodological fields because the document is a descriptive OECD country note that compiles Education at a Glance 2025 indicators. It does not conduct an original student-level analysis, does not specify an analytic sample of students, and does not report any ML model training, validation metrics, or PV-based achievement scaling. Consequently, fields such as plausible values handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not part of the note’s methodology; the relevant technical details are instead provided in the referenced OECD sources/methodologies documentation.
